title: The Apocalypse of Abraham
author: G. H. Box (trans)
description: The Apocalypse of Abraham, edited with a translation from the Slavonic text and notes by G. H. Box with J. I. Landsman (London: SPCK, 1918), in the 'Translations of Early Documents, Series I: Palestinian Jewish Texts (Pre-Rabbinic)'. Surviving only in Old Church Slavonic but originally a Jewish work of the late first or early second century CE, written after the destruction of the Temple, it has two parts. The first is a haggadic story of the young Abraham in his father Terah's idol workshop, discovering the folly of idolatry and the true God. The second is an apocalypse: guided by the angel Yahoel, Abraham offers sacrifice and ascends on the wings of a bird to the heavenly throne, where he sees the fiery chariot (Merkavah), the creation, the fall caused by the fallen angel Azazel, the history of Israel and the judgement to come. It is an important link between apocalyptic and Merkavah mysticism.
